clue.text: Hard current measures, with Tory PM impounding a green urban area

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
amps measure electric current

indicators.note: impounding means shutting something up inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Ted Heath, Conservative Prime Minister 1970-74

explanation.surface: An electricity report: hard measurements of current, while a Conservative prime minister locks away a patch of parkland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tory PM is given in full, first name and surname together, and 'impounding' puts A inside that name. Hampstead Heath is a large park in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: This London heath is a famous expanse of open parkland inside the city, a green space amid streets.

clue.text: Criminal's speech, cunning, filled with energy

indicators.note: a word filled with something has that thing put inside it

parts.note: cunning or craft can be called art
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A crook talks slyly and with plenty of vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: This term covers the private jargon or slang of a group, classically the underworld's cant.

clue.text: Stone lots of people cut from excavator

parts.note: a pit is the stone of a fruit such as a cherry

indicators.note: cut means docked of its last letter here

parts.note: many means a large number of people

explanation.surface: Someone stones a crowd that has been separated from a digging machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone' is the fruit kernel, not the weight or the rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal miner works digging underground, so he is literally a digger or excavator.

clue.text: Exaggerated two articles with another article unfinished, sadly

parts.note: the and a are the definite and indefinite articles
the second of the two articles is the indefinite one

indicators.note: sadly signals that the letters are in a sorry, jumbled state
unfinished means the last letter is lost

parts.note: the word itself is taken as written

explanation.surface: A grammarian laments overdone writing with two articles and a third left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' leaves ARTICL, and 'sadly' rearranges those letters; 'another' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical behaviour is overdone and showy, as on stage, so it means exaggerated or melodramatic.

clue.text: Cautious, with setback in first half? Not true

indicators.note: setback here applies only to the opening two letters, which are turned round

parts.note: wary means cautious

explanation.surface: A wary person with an early-season setback finds the reports false.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half, WA, is turned to AW; RY stays.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew is not straight or true, as with a crooked picture or a plan gone wrong.

clue.text: Slow down man with a capacity to forestall decision?

parts.note: he is the male pronoun, standing for a man
a veto is the power to block a decision

explanation.surface: A man with blocking powers puts the brakes on a decision.
explanation.walkthrough: A nautical phrase: a ship heaves to by turning into the wind to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors bring a vessel to a halt or near-standstill this way, so it means to stop or slow down.

clue.text: A fight with a severe blow would be more than enough for this spear-carrier

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do

indicators.note: the full word is one letter more than needed, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a gust is a strong blast of wind

explanation.surface: A spear-carrying warrior faces a fight and a heavy blow, which would be overkill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spear-carrier' looks like a soldier or an extra on stage, but the vegetable grows in spears.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable is sold and eaten as spears, so the plant carries spears in a witty sense.

clue.text: Screwed up marginal then weakened government?

indicators.note: screwed means twisted or messed about, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A party blew a marginal seat and the resulting government was weak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' belongs to the fodder, not to 'Screwed up'.
explanation.definitionFit: When no party has a majority in the House, the result is a weak administration without full control.

clue.text: Manila, as it were, in film comedy

parts.note: read the solution as an instruction: the first word gone crazy gives the Philippine capital

explanation.surface: A Philippine city appears, as it were, in a slapstick movie.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'crackers' (crazy) is an anagram signal working on the first word, which gives the city.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a 1930 Marx Brothers picture, a classic screen farce.

clue.text: Little good in tossing and turning in the raw — try this!

definitions.text: Little good in tossing and turning in the raw — try this!

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
tossing and turning suggests restless rearrangement of the letters

parts.note: G is the short form of good

explanation.surface: Advice to a restless naked sleeper: pyjamas might help.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyjamas and nighties are what one wears in bed, the alternative to sleeping naked.

clue.text: One's nearly exhausted, reaching city in Colorado

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article

indicators.note: nearly means short of the last letter

parts.note: spent means exhausted

explanation.surface: A tired traveller is almost worn out on arriving in a Rocky Mountain resort.
explanation.definitionFit: This ski resort is a well-known small city in the Rocky Mountain state.

clue.text: Satisfied with performers in weather programme

parts.note: met as in met demands, satisfied them
the cast is the group of performers

explanation.surface: A happy viewer enjoys the presenters of a weather show.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a meteorological forecast broadcast, a forecast bulletin on radio or TV.

clue.text: Carried over surplus

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ported means carried, as a rifle is

explanation.surface: Accounts language: the excess is carried forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A French loan phrase meaning too much, unwanted or superfluous, applied to someone not welcome.

clue.text: Parisian is involved in supporting curtailed budget

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: shoring means propping up, supporting
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A Frenchman helps prop up a cut-back budget.
explanation.definitionFit: A budget run on very little money is said to be on a tiny one, a slender allowance.

clue.text: Prison removing first component of chains

indicators.note: removing first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: clink is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A jail that takes the first prisoner out of chains.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain is a series of these rings joined together, each one a single loop.

clue.text: Wild iguana seizing vehicle in American region

indicators.note: seizing means taking hold of, so the other piece goes inside
wild means uncontrolled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A wild lizard grabs a car somewhere in the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: This republic lies in Central America, an area of the American continent.

clue.text: Quiet method of working brought in to identify tradesman

indicators.note: brought in means put within the other word

parts.note: to finger someone is to identify them to police
sh is the call for quiet
MO is modus operandi, method of working

explanation.surface: Police quietly bring in an informer to identify a merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller of fish is a trader or shopkeeper, a type of retail tradesman.

clue.text: Hymn's way to show sea and fog?

parts.note: read the title as an instruction: shaking up its last two words spells a mist over water, the sea and fog of the clue

explanation.surface: A hymn depicting a misty seascape.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the title as 'rock OF AGES', with rock as an anagram signal; OF AGES shaken gives SEA FOG, which the clue spells out as 'sea and fog'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known Christian hymn by Augustus Toplady, sung in churches.

clue.text: Unpopular farm produce in unexpected area of land

parts.note: out means unfashionable, unpopular
a crop is what a farm produces

explanation.surface: A disliked harvest in a surprising field.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock that appears at the surface is a sudden exposed patch of ground amid soil.

clue.text: Bubbly stuff, mostly buzzing

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: astir means busy and buzzing

explanation.surface: Fizzy drink mostly buzzing with bubbles.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian sparkling wine is a classic fizz, popular with crossword setters.

clue.text: Sheep, second that Ireland's brought in

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second
Erin is a poetic name for Ireland

explanation.surface: A second flock of sheep that Ireland has imported.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed of fine-wooled livestock is prized for its soft fleece.

clue.text: Clergyman prompt to restrain scoundrel

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so the other word goes inside

parts.note: a cue is a prompt to an actor
a rat is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A vicar is quick to hold back a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant parish priest in the Church of England is a junior member of the clergy.

clue.text: Hypothesis in that situation involving old money

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the other piece goes within

parts.note: there means in that place or situation

explanation.surface: A theory about a situation involving old cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition that can be proved is a formal statement, near in sense to a thesis or proposition.

clue.text: Queen elevated in restricting Government's time in power

indicators.note: elevated in a down entry means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: taken as written
G is short for government

explanation.surface: A queen raised to the throne curbs the government's term.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's period on the throne is the time he or she rules.

clue.text: Firm invested in fashionable film star?

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, like money

parts.note: in means fashionable
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company puts money into a trendy movie celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated screen idol is a cultural idol, a revered figure.

clue.text: Inventor of counting device heading off for mountain

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Hans Geiger co-invented the Geiger counter

explanation.surface: A scientist sets off for an alpine peak.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a famous peak in the Bernese Alps of Switzerland, known for its north face.

clue.text: I note big company brought in family doctor

indicators.note: brought in means put within the other word

parts.note: a clan is a family group
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a big British firm

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a large firm has brought in a family GP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family' belongs to the wordplay, not to 'family doctor'.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical practitioner who sees patients is a physician working in a clinical setting.

clue.text: Covert scheme involving a politician broke up favourite spot

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a sting is an undercover police operation
MP is a Member of Parliament
ground means broke up into small pieces

explanation.surface: An undercover plot against a politician ruins someone's beloved haunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's old haunt is the place they regularly frequent, their favourite haunt.
